subject: Pod alignment proposal + review cadence for inference platform
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, PeopleShift Consulting <jenna@peopleshift.co>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Pod alignment proposal + review cadence for inference platform

Team — attaching a short rationale and role matrix for the proposed pod alignment across the inference platform org. TL;DR: move from three horizontally-scoped squads (Edge, Serving, Platform Tools) to four product-aligned pods (Serving Core, Serving Scale, Developer Platform, Edge & Integrations) with a single tech lead per pod and dotted-line reporting for infra engineers.

Why now: delivery fragmentation, slow cross-pod rollouts, and uneven performance review signals (same rubric but different expectations). I tried to balance throughput risk vs. career scaffolding — the deck spells out tradeoffs and a two-phase rollout (opt-in pilot in Q1 then full move by end of Q2).

Key asks in this thread:
- Quick sanity check from Marcus & Lauren on the pod boundaries and manager load.
- Aditya: I want your view on review cadence (aligned to compensation cycle vs. steady quarterly calibration).
- Monica: confirm constraints for headcount moves, comp committee timing, and any notice requirements.

Attachments: reorg_rationale_deck.pdf (12 slides), role_matrix_v2.xlsx (proposed titles/IC->manager mapping).

Next steps I propose in the doc: pilot Serving Scale + Developer Platform with 2 pods and 3-month pilot metrics (deployment time, incident MTTR, cross-pod PR lead time).

Thanks — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Product, Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Pod alignment proposal + review cadence for inference platform

Kimberly — skimmed the deck and role matrix. High-level thumbs up on splitting Serving into Core vs Scale; that matches where ops vs infra specializations are diverging. A couple of quick notes:
- Manager spans: make sure the new tech lead role is explicit about 1:1 IC mentoring time — we lost that when spans crept up last year.
- Pilot metrics: add a developer productivity metric (PR review cycle) and customer-impacting latency regressions (5xxs by deploy).

I can sync with you Monday to map on-call and escalation.

—Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, PeopleShift Consulting <jenna@peopleshift.co>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pod alignment proposal + review cadence for inference platform

Appreciate the thoughtfulness here. A few operational questions and comms asks before we take this broader:

1) Manager load: what temporary coverage do we need for the two-week carveout period when some managers will be heavily involved in the pilot? (I don't want escalation gaps.)
2) Role names/titles in the matrix — please mark which are promotions vs. lateral moves so we can prep compensation notes.
3) Comms: recommend a two-step announcement — (a) cross-functional heads + pilot teams this week, (b) company town hall the week after pilot kickoff. Monica — can you flag any legal/notice items?

I can draft the email for (a) once you confirm the pilot roster. Also, on review cadence: if we make performance signals more frequent (quarterly touchpoints + mid-year calibration), we need a lightweight scorecard for managers to keep consistency.

—Lauren
VP, People Ops

---

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pod alignment proposal + review cadence for inference platform

Kimberly / all — my two cents on cadence: keep the formal comp cycle synced to existing annual timeline to avoid budgeting churn, but add quarterly calibration checkpoints that are explicitly "developmental/feedback" focused (no comp decisions). That lets managers correct course faster and reduces surprises at annual calibration.

Operationally: the pilot should include a shared rubric for scoring cross-pod contributors (SLO ownership, service reliability, delivery impact). I can work with Marcus to bake a short rubric and a one-pager for managers.

Also: consider making the pilot pods limited to 6 months if the metrics are conservative; that gives time to observe real rollout behavior across releases.

—Aditya
VP, Engineering

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pod alignment proposal + review cadence for inference platform

Thanks for the context — a few HR/legal constraints to call out upfront:

- Any reporting-line changes that are title reductions or that materially change job scope require 2 weeks' advance notice to the impacted employees and a conversation with People Ops. If the move is a promotion or lateral change, we should still document the new scope and adjust comp where appropriate.
- If the plan touches contractors/temps, confirm status early — we may need SOW amendments.
- Comp committee: the next window for budgeted comp changes is Feb 15, 2027. Anything that requires comp uplift to make the new role competitive needs pre-approval by Jan 20 to get on the Feb packet.
- Confidentiality: avoid broad distribution of the role matrix until offers/promotions are signed — leak risk is real.

Operational asks from HR: please provide pilot roster and the list of impacted roles by Dec 6. I'll run headcount and any necessary notice language, and loop Legal for SOW/contract items. Jenna from PeopleShift — can you review the comms cadence and provide a short template for the pilot announcement? Avalon Legal — please flag any employment-law concerns for the EU nodes if this touches Amsterdam or Berlin headcount (we haven't yet, but flagging proactively).

—Monica
Director, People Operations (HR)

Appreciate the quick feedback — summary & actions: 

1) Pilot roster & roles: I'll circulate the suggested pilot roster and mark promotions vs lateral moves by EOD Dec 3.
2) Metrics & rubric: Marcus + Aditya to co-own the pilot rubric (PR cycle time, deploy success rate, incident MTTR, customer latency regressions). Deliverable: one-pager by Dec 7.
3) HR/comms: Monica to confirm legal/notices and comp constraints (Dec 6). Monica to review the comms templates from Jenna.
4) Timing: pilot kickoff Jan 10 (2 pods) — pilot length 3 months with a check-in at 6 weeks. We'll decide on full roll by April 1.

Related links: pilot plan doc (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AaExampleDoc), Jira SUP-1234 for staging infra work, confluence plan page above.

If no objections, I'll send the targeted pilot announcement to the heads-of-product list tomorrow and we can finalize the roster.

Thanks — Kimberly
Head of Product, Inference
Redwood Inference
